text:
carol: Heads-up — after the 03/15 outage we had a lot of dropped follow-ups. Can we try a small pilot for an automated postmortem scheduler + handoff timer bot?
rohan: +1. we lose momentum when the oncall hands off and no owner is assigned. what do you have in mind?
emily: curious how this would differ from calendar invites + reminders. sounds noisy if it fires for every page. :thinking_face:
dave: idea: severity-based triggers. only auto-schedule for sev2+ and when customer-impact flag is set. lower sev => just a DM reminder.
carol: exactly. MVP: bot creates a calendar invite, posts a short postmortem template link, and opens a tracking card in our action dashboard with an owner (defaults to the primary oncall). timer keeps the handoff visible for 24h.
rohan: love the default owner idea. we should also auto-populate customer impact summary from incident report so we don't lose context. ops-bot could surface the summarized impact lines.
ops-bot: incident detected: INC-2026-0315. severity=2. affected-customers=3. summarizing recent notes...
ops-bot: summary: "API gateway overload from malformed bulk requests → partial degradation for partner integrations. mitigation: rate-limit and patch rolled at 03:42 UTC."
emily: nic e. if the bot auto-creates the PM, can it also attach the relevant logs/links? even just the top 3 links would help.
rohan: technical ask: need sane opt-out for teams who do their own postmortems. maybe a channel-level setting or an ‘exclude-tag’.
dave: agree. also we should avoid duplicate invites if someone manually schedules. bot should check for existing PMs with the same incident id.
carol: here's a quick command sketch for the bot UX: 
```
/sched-pm INC-2026-0315 --owner @rohan --when tomorrow 15:00UTC --severity 2
```
carol: Bot response should be short: "Scheduled postmortem invite for INC-2026-0315 (owner @rohan) — calendar + card created. Reply `!claim` to reassign."
rohan: nice. can we also add a small interactive checklist in the card: impact, timeline, root cause, remediation, follow-ups? and a field for estimated customer notification status.
emily: +1 to checklist. also add a 'blocker' flag so status pages can surface outstanding customer communications.
dave: from infra side: the bot should respect oncall rotation metadata. i can add an endpoint that returns current primary.
carol: implementation notes: 1) hook into pagerduty/pagerbot to get incident id + severity 2) create calendar invite + postmortem doc template (drive link) 3) create an action-board card and attach checklist 4) tag current oncall as default owner 5) post summary into the incident channel
rohan: timeline for pilot? i can build a prototype that does steps 1+2 this sprint, then we can add action-board integration next sprint.
emily: can we make the postmortem template lightweight? people skip long forms. maybe a 6-field quick form then expandable.
carol: agreed. quick form fields: short impact blurb, timeline bullets, root cause short sentence, remediation items (3 max), owner, follow-up due date.
ops-bot: suggestion: add a 24h handoff timer. if the owner isn't confirmed within 12h, ping oncall lead and escalate. if not confirmed within 48h, mark as "needs assignment" and page oncall rota.
rohan: escalation flow seems fair. avoid noisy pages for small incidents. keep it sev-based.
dave: ops concern: who maintains the bot? we need a small runbook for failures (e.g., calendar API rate limits). I can draft a resilience checklist.
emily: propose we run pilot for 4 weeks in eng-oncall only, measure: PM scheduled rate, actions created, and % of actions resolved within SLO.
carol: ok. volunteers for pilot: rohan (prototype), dave (infra integration), emily (UX + metrics). i'll coordinate the rollout and write the quick runbook. :+1:
rohan: i'll open a tracking issue and put a prototype branch on github: rwd/postmortem-bot-proto.
carol: thanks — i'll add coordination notes to the action-board and schedule a 30m sync to demo next Tue 14:00 UTC.
pagerbot: reminder scheduled: "postmortem-bot pilot demo" Tue 14:00 UTC — added to eng-oncall calendar.
emily: sweet. low-friction first step is best. excited to try it. :rocket:
